Thanks for the PR and for getting confirmation from WebKit! Lightning CSS already adds `-webkit-text-size-adjust` whenever your targets include iOS Safari. For example, with `ios_saf 17` (or the browserslist `defaults` query) you get:

```css
.foo{-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;text-size-adjust:none}
```

Desktop Safari doesn't support `text-size-adjust` at all, so targets like `safari 17` alone don't add it. If you're not seeing the prefix, please check that your targets include iOS Safari (e.g. `ios_saf >= 16`); some tools only pass desktop browsers by default. Adding the prefix for every target would also emit it for browsers that never need it, so I'm going to close this one.
